title: Your Agents Need a Save Button - Hamza Tahir, ZenML
talk_summary: He demos Kitaru: replay one run, replay a cohort of expensive/long runs, diff side-by-side, and use an MCP server + LLM to analyze the cohort report — warning that single replays are anecdotes and naive model swaps are often a false economy.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of trusting one replay, they replay a cohort of real production runs (e.g. the most expensive/longest) with the cheaper model and diff outcomes against baseline before routing traffic.
takeaways.evidence_quote: one replay is just an anecdote and having a cohort analysis is way way way better
takeaways.numbers: Model passing 60% of the time is self-consistent only ~25% of the time; DoorDash: hours→5 min, 90% less hallucination, within 2 points of production

takeaways.evidence_quote: the first three checkpoints are skipped ... All it needs to do is just change this particular checkpoint

takeaways.technique: MCP server over run/cohort reports for LLM analysis
takeaways.what_they_do: Emit cohort replay results as JSON and expose a runtime MCP server so an agent can query executions, fetch artifacts, and flag red flags across thousands of runs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: use the Kitaru MCP server ... read this JSON report and do an analysis on what you think I should be doing across the cohort

takeaways.technique: Target replays at expensive/long/risky runs only
takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly scope replay cohorts to the runs that matter (expensive, slow, risky) because replaying everything is too costly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: This can get very expensive of course and this is where you have to be really smart about what you replay

takeaways.what_they_do: Checkpoints capture the environment (Docker image or sandbox) alongside code and artifacts, so replay reproduces the exact runtime.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the environment in which it ran in, whether it was a Docker image or a sandbox, those are all snapshotted in state
